3aed3527b5.q: What are the four levels of AI implementation in product onboarding according to Delight Path?
3aed3527b5.a: The four levels are: AI tells (chatbots providing information from knowledge base), AI guiding (launching tours and in-app patterns to guide users toward specific goals using tools like AppCue's and UserFlow), AI generating (creating custom-built templates for specific users based on their needs), and AI acting (AI agents performing actions on behalf of users, like Salesforce Agent Force or QuickBooks invoice creation).
3aed3527b5.e: How AI is changing user onboarding, one level at a time | Ramli John (Delight Path)
3aed3527b5.rq: AI is essentially just an average of whatever's online. And there are insights outside of the average in the world that you can truly bring into your product, product design, your user experience and everything else.

f2db2ca77b.q: How should product teams train and improve their taste and delight skills?
f2db2ca77b.a: Taste is built through experience and analyzing what you like and don't like in the market. It requires connecting with customers to understand their emotional responses and expectations. Human connection with both customers and industry peers is critical—connecting with other product leaders helps you gain taste from others, similar to how chefs learn nuances from other foodies. This peer connection is more important than ever amid AI hype.

ccc7eba52d.q: What is the difference between how Notion users and ZenMate users perceive delight?
ccc7eba52d.a: Notion users might find visual delight like animations and guidance delightful, while ZenMate customers (cleaning business owners) are busy and prefer getting what they need right now without extra interface elements. What one customer base finds delightful, another might find annoying enough to leave the product. Understanding who you are serving is essential to define appropriate delight.

4c833e4c7d.q: How does exceeding user expectations define product delight?
4c833e4c7d.a: Delight is about surprising users by exceeding their set expectations. Ramli John's example is Uber: users expected flagging a cab would take a while and require paying with a credit card, but instead they just got in, got out, and didn't have to pay—exceeding expectations created that moment of delight and surprise.

f645b5541f.q: Why do AI companies need to build in-person communities according to product leaders?
f645b5541f.a: As AI becomes more prevalent, human connection becomes the differentiator. In-person communities and real-life interactions help verify authenticity—you can tell if you're talking to a real person versus AI. AI is essentially just an average of whatever is online, but human insights and conversations reveal perspectives outside of that average that can truly improve product design and user experience.
